title: Base previewExitFor's netGuaranteed is a ceiling, not a floor, when the share-balance cap binds (direct strategy)
description: The base default at AYieldStrategy.sol:571-583 computes grossToRequest = min(netWanted, clientBalances[token][account]) and then sets netGuaranteed = grossToRequest, i.e. it quotes booked principal rather than deliverable underlying. It does not model the vault share balance at all, so when the position is below par the published 'guarantee' is a ceiling on what can be delivered rather than a floor beneath it. Reached in production through ERC4626YieldStrategy, which does not override the base.
impact: The direct strategy's published exit floor over-states deliverable underlying by the full vault deficit: 1000e18 quoted, 500e18 delivered after a 50% drawdown. The function's own NatSpec uses the word 'guarantees'. Filed at Low because previewExitFor has zero consumers at every sibling repo's current top-level HEAD (verified three times independently, untruncated), so the mis-quote is consumed by nobody today.
attackPath: A client is credited principal p on ERC4626YieldStrategy.
The wired ERC4626 vault falls below par (50% drawdown in the PoC).
An integrator STATICCALLs previewExitFor(token, client, p) and is told netGuaranteed == p == 1000e18.
withdraw() delivers 500e18 while debiting the full requested amount at AYieldStrategy.sol:781-783.
No revert, no event: the shortfall is silent.
recommendation: Model the share balance in the base preview as the market override's _exitFloor does — cap netGuaranteed by the underlying realizable from vault.convertToAssets(min(convertToShares(gross), balanceOf(strategy))) — or, at minimum, strike the word 'guarantees' from the NatSpec and document the return as a non-binding upper estimate. NOTE (non-collapse, load-bearing): a fix that merely copies _exitFloor into the base closes this finding and SPREADS L-20 to the direct strategy; the two must be fixed together.
evidenceBasis: 696 M-state exhaustive integer search of the live semantics (210 M cap-binding states, 0 counterexamples), 4 M random samples at 2^90 magnitudes, 150 k fuzz + a 105-case grid against the real contracts in the real two-client topology, with live vacuity tripwires (one fired and caught a vacuous first harness). NOT a Halmos proof — the symbolic tier returned 0 [PASS] / 7 [TIMEOUT]. Never write 'symbolically verified'.
escalationTrigger: (a) WATCH-17-03 — stable-staker bumps lib/reflax-yield-vault to a story-050 commit and gates a user-facing path on netGuaranteed; OR (b) either dominance invariant (AYieldStrategy.sol:48 totalDeposited == sum(clientBalances); :772-776 withdraw amount capped to available principal) ceases to hold. Either => Medium.
dominanceContingency: MR-17-05: the StableStakerV2._isUnderwater dominance that holds this at Low rests on two invariants NO test pins (AYieldStrategy.sol:48 and :772-776). A future change breaking either re-arms this at Medium WITH NO SCANNER SIGNAL. DominanceRun17Grounding.t.sol is the runnable regression guard and should be kept.
nonCollapse: Must NOT absorb L-20 (DEDUP-17-03). This is the base not modelling the share cap at all; L-20 is the market override modelling it correctly and still being wrong across clients.
